references.text: Moses announces the Lord's judgment on the firstborn in Egypt, which is fulfilled in 12:12
The fulfillment of the Lord's promise to strike down all the firstborn in Egypt
The Egyptians buried their firstborn whom the Lord had struck, and the Lord executed judgment against their gods
The Lord takes the Levites instead of all the firstborn in Israel, who were spared in Egypt
The psalmist recalls how God struck down all the firstborn in Egypt
The Lord struck down all the firstborn in their land, the firstfruit of all their strength
The Lord struck down the firstborn of Egypt, both human and animal
The Lord struck Egypt through their firstborn, for his mercy endures forever
The Lord's judgment against the idols of Egypt—they tremble before his presence
The Lord visits Amon of No and the gods of Egypt
The Lord executes judgment on Egypt
By faith Moses kept the Passover and applied the blood, so that the destroyer would not touch their firstborn
Numbers 3:13 interprets the historical event in Exodus 12 as the basis for the consecration of Israel's firstborn.
The judgment on the firstborn (Ex 12) is the concrete action that fulfills God's promise to take Israel for himself (Ex 6).
Exodus 3:20 prophesies about the hand reaching out against Egypt, which is concretely fulfilled in the judgment on the firstborn in Exodus 12.
Exodus 7:5 sets out God's purpose with the hand against Egypt, which culminates in the judgment on the firstborn in Exodus 12.
